passage: Harwick, Tuesday. The Calder Street bridge will close to all traffic on March 14 while county crews replace its corroded deck plates, the Harwick roads office said on Monday. The closure is expected to last eleven weeks, with reopening penciled in for the first week of June. Repairs will cost 1.8 million dollars, a figure the county negotiated down from an initial contractor bid of 2.4 million dollars submitted last autumn. During the work, drivers will be routed along Mercer Avenue, a detour that adds roughly nine minutes to a typical crossing. Cyclists and pedestrians will keep a narrow protected lane on the bridge itself for the first three weeks, after which they too will be diverted. Roads supervisor Alma Reyes told the council that the deck plates, installed in 1987, had worn thinner than inspections in 2019 suggested. The council approved the closure by a vote of six to two. Local merchants asked for signs directing customers to the Calder Street shops, and the county agreed to install eight signs before work begins.
question: How much will the Calder Street bridge repairs cost?

passage: Dellmore, Friday. A fire that began shortly after 4 a.m. gutted the kitchen of the Copper Kettle bakery on Winslow Road, though the shopfront and the apartment above it were saved. Fire crews from two stations reached the scene within eight minutes of the alarm and had the blaze contained by 5:20 a.m. Investigators traced the fire to a faulty proofing cabinet, ruling out an early suspicion that a wiring fault in the basement was to blame. Owner Teodor Malik estimated the damage at 90,000 dollars, most of it from the loss of two deck ovens imported four years ago at a cost of 31,000 dollars each. No one was injured, although one firefighter was treated at the scene for smoke exposure and released. The bakery employs eleven people, and Malik said he intends to keep paying all of them while the kitchen is rebuilt. He hopes to reopen within ten weeks, selling a reduced range from a rented cart outside the shop in the meantime. The last serious fire on Winslow Road was in 2011.
question: What did investigators identify as the cause of the bakery fire?
distractors: a wiring fault in the basement

passage: Voters in the town of Brenner Falls elected Ida Kessling as mayor on Thursday, ending a campaign dominated by argument over the future of the Wren Street depot. Kessling took 4,912 votes against 3,377 for the incumbent, Marcus Bright, who had held the office for two terms. A third candidate, Perry Okafor, drew 1,140 votes on a platform of merging the town's two fire districts. Turnout was 58 percent of registered voters, the highest for a town election since 1994. Kessling, a retired surveyor, campaigned on converting the depot into a covered market rather than selling the land to a storage company, the plan Bright had supported. She will be sworn in on the second Monday of January. In her remarks at the community hall, Kessling thanked her volunteers, numbering about 130 by her campaign's own count, and said her first act would be to order an independent appraisal of the depot site. Bright congratulated her before midnight and said he would return to his engineering practice.
question: How many votes did Ida Kessling receive?

passage: The Aldergate public library reopened on Saturday after a two year expansion that doubled its floor space and added a children's wing shaped like the hull of a boat. The project cost 6.3 million dollars, funded by a bond approved in a close referendum and by a 750,000 dollar gift from the estate of a former schoolteacher, Nella Vaughn. The building was designed by the architect Ruben Castell, whose firm won the commission over eleven other entrants in a juried competition. The most debated feature, a reading tower with a spiral stair, survived three budget reviews largely intact, losing only its planned copper roof. Head librarian Simone Duarte said circulation had been running at about 9,000 items a month before construction and that she expects the figure to pass 14,000 within a year. The library will now open on Sundays for the first time in its history. A ribbon was cut at noon by the town's oldest cardholder, aged 101, who borrowed a book of tide tables.
question: Who designed the expanded Aldergate public library?

passage: A line of storms crossed Perrin County late on Wednesday, toppling trees and cutting power to about 21,000 homes at the peak of the outages. The weather office recorded a top gust of 74 miles per hour at the Danby airfield, the strongest reading in the county since 2008. Most of the damage was concentrated in the townships of Loum and Sader Creek, where a machine shed collapsed and two grain bins were rolled into a fence line. No injuries were reported, though a delivery driver was briefly trapped when a maple fell across both lanes of Route 9 and pinned his van by the rear doors. Utility crews from three neighboring counties began arriving before dawn, and by Thursday evening the number of homes without power had fallen to 2,600. County engineer Willa Trask said the Route 9 culvert, already scheduled for replacement, had washed out and would be bypassed with a temporary steel span within a week. Cleanup costs are provisionally estimated at 1.1 million dollars.
question: What was the strongest wind gust recorded during the storm?

passage: The Fenwick High robotics team returned from the Tri-Basin regional on Sunday with the top prize and a place in the national finals, the first in the school's history. The team, which competes under the name Iron Herons, finished the elimination rounds with a score of 212, nineteen points clear of the runners-up from Castlereagh Academy. Their machine, a low chassis with a folding arm nicknamed the Preacher, was rebuilt twice during the season after a gearbox failure in October and a controller fault in January. Team captain Rosa Imbe, a senior, credited the win to a decision made in November to switch from treads to wheels, which cut the robot's turning time nearly in half. The squad numbers fourteen students and two volunteer mentors, one a retired toolmaker and the other a nurse who handles logistics. The national finals will be held in April, and the team must raise about 8,000 dollars for travel. A booster breakfast is planned at the fire hall on the first Saturday of March.
question: What score did the Iron Herons finish with in the elimination rounds?

passage: A new ferry service between Cobalt Bay and the island village of Stray Point begins on the first of May, restoring a link that lapsed nine years ago when the old operator gave up the route. The service will run four crossings a day in each direction in summer, dropping to two in winter, with the last departure from the island at 6:40 p.m. Fares are set at 7 dollars for adults and 3 dollars for children, with a monthly pass at 95 dollars aimed at commuters. The vessel, a 62 foot catamaran named the Gannet, carries 90 passengers and up to a dozen bicycles but no cars. The operator, a cooperative of island residents formed two winters ago, raised 400,000 dollars in member shares and secured the rest of the purchase price with a harbor authority loan. Crossing time is 35 minutes. Schedules will be posted at both piers and in the village store. The cooperative says the route will break even at 41,000 riders a year, a figure the old service last reached in 2013.
question: What is the name of the vessel on the new ferry route?

passage: Crews worked through Tuesday night to repair a burst water main under Larch Street that left 340 households dry and closed the street to traffic for most of a day. The cast iron main, laid in 1931, split along a six foot seam near the corner of Larch and Pomeroy, sending water into basements on the downhill side of the block. The utility opened a temporary standpipe outside the Larch Street chapel and handed out bottled water from a trailer, a supply that ran out once and was restocked from the depot in Girard. Service was restored to most homes by 4 p.m. on Wednesday, though eleven houses closest to the break stayed on a boil water notice for another two days as a precaution. A utility spokesman, Corin Aldous, said the section that failed had been scheduled for relining in three years under the current replacement plan, which covers about two miles of pipe a year. The repair itself cost roughly 60,000 dollars, not counting claims for flooded basements, of which nineteen had been filed by Friday.
question: In what year was the water main under Larch Street laid?

passage: The Marrow Hill museum announced on Thursday that it has acquired the painting Low Tide at Erskine, a harbor scene by the painter Casimir Volle, for 240,000 dollars. The purchase was funded half by the museum's acquisition endowment and half by a gift from the shipping heir Lionel Damaris, whose family once owned the wharf shown at the left edge of the canvas. The museum outbid two private collectors at auction, where the work had been estimated to sell for as little as 150,000 dollars. Volle painted the scene in 1911 from the window of a harbormaster's office, and the picture stayed in the harbormaster's family for three generations before surfacing at a regional sale in 2019. Curator Bette Onwudiwe said the painting will hang in the east gallery beside the museum's two other Volle works, both gifts from the same 1968 bequest. The frame, judged not original, will be replaced with a period-correct one built by the museum's own workshop. An unveiling is set for the second Friday of next month.
question: How much did the museum pay for Low Tide at Erskine?

passage: Nearly 2,300 runners finished Sunday's Redgate marathon under a low gray sky, and the men's and women's winners both broke course records that had stood for over a decade. Elias Munro crossed first in 2 hours 19 minutes 44 seconds, carving almost two minutes off the old mark set in 2012. The women's race went to Priya Chandrasekar in 2 hours 38 minutes 5 seconds, ahead of the defending champion, Greta Halvorsen, who finished third after losing a shoe at the second water station and stopping to relace it. Organizers said 2,940 runners had registered, meaning about one in five did not finish or did not start, a typical share for the course, whose long climb at mile 19 is locally nicknamed the Grindstone. The race raised 76,000 dollars for the county ambulance fund, up from 61,000 dollars last year. Munro, a schoolteacher who trains before dawn, said he had entered mainly to pace a friend and only decided to race at the halfway mark. Next year's edition is set for the last Sunday of September.
question: Who won the women's race at the Redgate marathon?
